title: Navigation and Workflow — How to Create Layers
description: Step-by-step workflows for the agent to create and configure layers on Resilience Atlas.

steps: 1. Verify S3 URI is accessible: use the titiler/info endpoint proxy to validate — GET /api/titiler/info?titilerUrl=<url>&cogUrl=<s3_uri>
2. Determine site_scope_id: ask user or call GET /api/admin/layers?collection=site_scopes
3. Determine layer_group_id: ask user or check existing layers in the same group
4. Build layer_config JSON for COG provider: {"body":{"source":"<s3_uri>","colormap_name":"<colormap>"}}
5. Set interaction_config to {} or a value output config
1. Import vector file to PostGIS: POST /api/admin/vector_tables/import with {"s3_uri":"<s3_uri>"}
1. Get WMS URL and LAYERS parameter from the data provider
1. Get the tile URL template with {z}/{x}/{y}

important_rules: slug must be globally unique across ALL layers. Check for conflicts before creating.
interaction_config is required — minimum value is '{}'.
layer_config must be valid JSON. Always validate JSON before sending.
Always link to a site_scope via site_scope_id parameter.
For martin layers, always import the vector table first using the vector_tables/import endpoint.
For COG layers, the S3 bucket is public-read — use s3:// URIs.
Never set layer_provider to 'leaflet', 'carto', 'cartodb', or 'raster' — these are deprecated.
authentication: Bearer token in Authorization header: 'Authorization: Bearer <RESILIENCE_API_KEY>'
